meta.description: Download a free Freelance Agreement template. Professional starting-point contract for freelance engagements. Covers deliverables, revisions, payment schedule, IP rights, and kill fee.

subtitle: A professional starting-point template for freelance engagements. Covers deliverables, revision rounds, payment milestones, IP transfer, and kill fee protection.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Deliverables & Acceptance
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Define exactly what 'done' looks like. Specify file formats, revision rounds, and acceptance criteria to avoid endless revisions.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Revision Rounds
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Limit included revisions (e.g., 2 rounds). Additional revisions should be billable at your hourly rate.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Payment Milestones
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Tie payments to milestones, not dates. Include deposit (25-50%) upfront. Final payment before final file delivery.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Kill Fee
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: If client cancels mid-project, you keep deposit + pay for work completed. Essential protection.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Intellectual Property
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: IP transfers upon FULL payment only. Until then, you retain copyright. Client gets license only after payment.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Portfolio Rights
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Retain right to showcase work in portfolio (with client approval for confidential projects).

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Late Payment
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Interest on overdue amounts + right to pause work until paid. Don't work for free.

faq.question: How many revision rounds should I include?
faq.answer: Standard is 2-3 rounds included in the base price. Additional rounds billed at your hourly rate. Define what counts as a 'round' (e.g., one consolidated feedback cycle).

faq.question: What is a kill fee and why do I need it?
faq.answer: A kill fee compensates you if the client cancels the project after you've started work. Typically: non-refundable deposit (25-50%) + payment for all work completed to date. Without it, you bear all risk of client cancellation.

faq.question: When does the client get copyright?
faq.answer: Only upon FULL payment. Until final payment clears, you retain copyright and the client has only a limited license. This is your primary leverage for getting paid.

faq.question: Can I use this for ongoing retainer work?
faq.answer: This template is designed for project-based engagements. For ongoing retainers, you need a different structure: monthly fee, scope cap, rollover terms, and termination notice periods.
